mechanism_narrative: The steady four-week recovery in RETAIL_REC from -33.0 to -22.7 reflects a continuing reopening trend driven by easing restrictions; this momentum should persist, pushing mean RETAIL_REC higher over the next 28 days relative to the last 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -33.0 to -22.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the last 28 days, reversing the established upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility rebounds above -20 points week-on-week, the return of commuting-linked foot traffic near offices will raise RETAIL_REC in the following two weeks as workers resume lunch and after-work shopping.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -20 points for at least one week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -32.3 to -21.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the two weeks following a WORKPLACES crossing above -20, or declines despite the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained high RESIDENTIAL mobility (above +10 for four consecutive weeks) indicates persistent caution and reduced discretionary outings, which will suppress RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks despite other reopening signals.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +10 for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 11.4 and 15.9 over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining elevated above +10 throughout the period.

mechanism_narrative: A TRANSIT recovery combined with a PARKS recovery indicates a broad resumption of outdoor and public mobility; when both series rise together week-on-week, RETAIL_REC tends to follow with a lagged increase within two weeks as combined mobility normalizes.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and PARKS both increase week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -59.1 to -51.0 and PARKS fluctuated with net rise from -35.7 to -21.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks of a joint TRANSIT-PARKS increase, or falls instead.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS decline in the most recent week (-12.3 to -21.4) after three weeks of recovery suggests a policy-driven tightening or weather-driven restriction on outdoor gathering that will also compress RETAIL_REC growth in the coming week as public caution increases.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 5 points week-on-week after a prior upward trend
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from -12.3 to -21.4 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise in the week following the PARKS reversal, showing no co-movement.

mechanism_narrative: The GROCERY_PHARM series has nearly normalized (-1.7 at t-0w), indicating essential-trip behavior has stabilized; because essential trips no longer substitute for discretionary retail visits, any further RETAIL_REC gains will depend on independent recovery in non-essential activity rather than spillover from grocery trips.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM near baseline at -1.7 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stagnates or declines even though GROCERY_PHARM remains near baseline, indicating no transfer of normalized essential mobility to discretionary retail.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility drops more than 10 points week-on-week (as seen from t-2w to t-1w, -25.6 to -31.7) while TRANSIT remains deeply negative, this signals a renewed restriction episode that will combine to suppress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks through reduced commuting-linked shopping.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 10 points week-on-week while TRANSIT remains below -50
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -25.6 to -31.7 while TRANSIT stayed near -54 to -55
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks despite the joint WORKPLACES drop and persistently low TRANSIT, invalidating the co-suppression mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-June timing coincides with seasonal summer leisure patterns in Madrid where PARKS and outdoor recreation typically rise independent of pandemic policy, and this seasonal pull will gradually shift discretionary trips toward outdoor parks rather than retail, keeping RETAIL_REC growth muted over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2020-06-15, early summer in Madrid
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in step with or faster than PARKS over the next four weeks, showing no seasonal substitution away from retail.
